identity_corrections: Year: evidence-card says 2022 (arXiv v1 date) → paper published at ICLR 2023. Minor discrepancy, arXiv submission date 2022 is correct but venue year is 2023.
abstract_snippet: We propose task vectors: directions in weight space obtained by subtracting pre-trained weights from fine-tuned weights. Task vectors can be modified and combined through arithmetic: negation (forgetting), addition (multi-task), and analogies (A:B::C:D). Operations are element-wise on model weights, with no extra inference cost. Experiments on CLIP, T5, and image classification show task arithmetic is simple, efficient, and effective.
what_the_paper_supports: Task vectors encode task-specific behavior as a direction in weight space (τ = θ_ft - θ_pre). Three arithmetic operations: (1) Negation (-τ) = forgetting/unlearning, (2) Addition (Στi) = multi-task model, (3) Analogy (τC + τB - τA) = transfer to task D. All operations are element-wise, no extra inference cost. Works across modalities (vision, language) and architectures (CLIP, T5). Key insight: task behavior is linearly encodable in weight space.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: No formal specification (GAP-015). No equivalence checking (GAP-017). No versioning (GAP-019). No formal verification (GAP-020). No execution trace. Only works with same architecture and same pre-trained init. Scaling λ requires validation data. No theoretical guarantee of arithmetic properties.
paper_core_claims: Task vector τ = θ_ft - θ_pre encodes task behavior as a direction in weight space
Negation (-τ) decreases target task performance with minimal control task impact
Addition (Στi) creates multi-task models competitive with specialized fine-tuned models
Task analogies (τC + τB - τA) improve performance on task D without D's training data
All operations are element-wise — no extra inference cost
Works across CLIP, T5, and multiple image classification tasks

GAP-016.reason: Task vectors as compiled task knowledge: fine-tuning compiles dataset → task vector → model. But compilation is just weight subtraction.

GAP-017.reason: Task arithmetic implies a form of algebraic equivalence: negation reverses, addition combines. But no formal equivalence checking.

GAP-019.reason: Task vectors as versionable, composable artifacts. Each task vector is a delta that can be stored, negated, added, combined. This is the most developed versioning/composition model in the batch — task vectors are explicitly treated as arithmetic objects that can be manipulated.

N2_Representation.reason: Task vector as weight-space representation of task behavior. Linear algebraic structure: negation, addition, analogy. This is the most mathematically structured representation of task knowledge in the batch — tasks are vectors in a vector space with arithmetic operations.

N3_Compiler.reason: Fine-tuning as compilation: dataset → task vector. But this is just gradient descent, not a compiler in the traditional sense.

N4_Artifact.reason: Task vectors as reusable, composable artifacts. Can be stored, shared, negated, added. Each task vector is a self-contained artifact encoding task behavior. Code released: https://github.com/mlfoundations/task_vectors

N7_Validator.reason: Validation accuracy for scaling λ. Control task accuracy to verify selectivity of negation. But no formal validation.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Task arithmetic IS composition: (1) negation = subtractive composition, (2) addition = additive composition, (3) analogy = relational composition (A:B::C:D). This is the most algebraically structured composition model in the batch — tasks are elements of a vector space with well-defined operations.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Task vectors as versionable deltas. Each vector is a diff from pre-trained model. Can be stored, retrieved, combined. This is a primitive but mathematically grounded versioning system — task vectors are the 'commits' and the pre-trained model is the 'base'.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Only works with same architecture and same pre-trained initialization
Scaling λ requires validation data — not truly zero-shot
No theoretical guarantee that arithmetic operations preserve model quality
Negation may have unintended side effects on control tasks
Addition may cause interference between tasks (negative transfer)
Analogy requires meaningful A:B::C:D relationship — not all tasks have this
Only tested on classification and generation tasks — unclear for other modalities
New parameters introduced during fine-tuning (e.g., classification heads) cannot be averaged
strengths_noted: N2 Representation: STRONGEST in batch — task vectors as elements of a vector space with arithmetic
N8 ComposerRouter: STRONGEST algebraic composition model — negation, addition, analogy
N9 VersionedRegistry: task vectors as diffs/commits — mathematically grounded versioning
N4 Artifact: composable, shareable, storable task vectors
Simple, fast, effective — element-wise operations, no extra training
Highly influential — spawned line of research on model merging/editing
